name: PT ABM Investama Tbk

frontmatter.title: ABM Investama — the parts are worth more than the holding
frontmatter.summary: ABM Investama is a family-controlled holding company whose listed GEMS stake is the largest part of a sum of the parts worth far more than the share price. The market applies a deep discount, and the house base rate says such discounts persist; our base therefore holds today's discount rather than banking a narrowing. At persistence the parts and the carry still support an ADD, with the narrowing as the bull case and the GEMS mark as the sized, unmodelled tail.
thesis: The market prices ABMM as a thermal-coal producer; on the audited numbers it is a holding company whose listed GEMS associate is the largest part and whose contractor, logistics and fabrication businesses earn fees.
The data pack understates depreciation by an order of magnitude; we restate D&A from the audited notes and rebuild EBITDA before valuing anything.

Our sum of the parts marks the operating segments on FY2025 through-cycle EBITDA net of the full SG&A charge, so the segment sum reconciles to consolidated EBITDA, and still sits far above the share price after a wide holdco discount.

The discount is the base rate, not the thesis: the house archetype puts narrowing at about one in three over three years, so the base holds today's market-implied discount and the narrowing is the bull case. The most-likely path supports ADD, not BUY.
GEMS is more than half the pre-discount NAV and is held at market in every scenario; a thermal-coal de-rating is the unmodelled tail, sized in section five rather than hidden.
Related-party revenue, the MDB transfer to a related party and the thin registry float are the governance risks that justify a discount wider than the peer modal level.

blocks.text: We initiate coverage of ABM Investama (ABMM), the listed holding company of the Tiara Marga Trakindo group, with a ADD rating and a twelve-month target of Rp2,764 against a last price of Rp2,540 — an expected total return of 12.9% including the Rp104 next-twelve-month dividend [S0, S12]. The company describes itself as an integrated energy group that invests across the mining value chain and across logistics, engineering and new businesses; it owns a mining contractor, a logistics and sea-transport cluster, a fabricator, a fuel trading book, three coal concessions and a portfolio of associates [S4, S8].

The variant view is a classification one, and it is the frame the Director's ruling requires. The market still prices ABMM as a thermal-coal producer with coal-price beta. On the audited numbers, however, the group's own coal sales are immaterial: its historic South Kalimantan mine's reserves were "fully depleted as of the end of December 2024" and it sold 0.3 Mt from that mine in FY2025 [S8]. What the group actually owns is a mining-contractor franchise, a fuel-trading book, a logistics and fabrication cluster, and — above all — a 30.0% associate stake in the listed coal producer PT Golden Energy Mines (GEMS) plus a remaining interest in the unlisted PT Media Djaya Bersama (MDB) [S12, S5]. Valued as a holding company rather than as a coal miner, the parts are worth far more than the holding: the engine marks the listed GEMS stake at GEMS's own market price, and that single mark is worth more than ABMM's entire market capitalisation.

Three things move the value. First, the GEMS mark: the listed associate's market price and the cash it upstreams are the largest single driver of the sum of the parts [S12]. Second, the holdco discount: today's price implies a discount of 66.2% to our pre-discount NAV, and our base applies the same 66.2%. That is deliberate. The house holdco-discount archetype puts narrowing at about one in three over three years, so the most-likely path is persistence, not a partial narrowing; the base is anchored to that branch and the dated events sit in the bull case [S13]. At persistence the parts and the carry still produce our ADD. Third, the operating EBITDA: the contractor and logistics segments earn at the EBITDA line, marked on FY2025 segment EBITDA after the full SG&A charge, and the coal-price cycle moves them less than it moves a pure producer [S12].

Two data corrections are central. The data pack carries a FY2025 depreciation figure that is a fraction of the audited charge, because it reads the single depreciation line inside general and administrative expenses of a direct-method filer [S0, S12]. We restate total D&A from the audited segment note — fixed assets, right-of-use assets and mining properties — and rebuild EBITDA from it; without that restatement the pack's EBITDA margin is materially wrong [S12, F17]. The same segment note defines segment EBITDA before SG&A, so we charge the consolidated SG&A and other operating expenses across the four operating segments before applying any multiple; the segment marks then sum to consolidated EBITDA instead of overstating it by the SG&A line [S12, F59, F60].

Our base case is the most likely path, not the cautious one: volumes and margins are held at the last actual, the GEMS mark is the market's own, the operating parts are marked at comp-supported multiples on true EBITDA, and the discount persists at the market-implied level. The scenarios flex the holdco discount, the only driver the sum of the parts can move; the GEMS mark and the segment marks are held in every scenario and their coal-price and related-party exposure is sized in section five rather than double-counted. The bear is now a genuine loss and the GEMS tail is quantified, not truncated. No third-party ratings, price objectives or published estimates were sought or used in this report; every number here is the house's own.

ABM Investama is an Indonesian integrated energy holding, listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange and part of the Tiara Marga Trakindo group [S4, S8]. It organises itself into two clusters: the Mining Value Chain, which gathers mining concessions, mining-contractor services, fuel management and coal shipping, and Logistics, Engineering and New Businesses, which gathers logistics, industrial engineering and renewable energy [S4]. Its operating subsidiaries include PT Cipta Kridatama (the mining contractor), PT Cipta Krida Bahari (logistics), PT Sanggar Sarana Baja (fabrication and equipment reconditioning), PT Reswara Minergi Hartama (the coal sub-holding) and PT Prima Wiguna Parama (fuel trading and services) [S12]. The 1H2026 corporate presentation sets out the same cluster structure, the shareholder composition and the operating footprint [S2].

The segment mix is the reason the coal-producer label is wrong. In FY2025 the group booked US$1,038.2m of consolidated revenue. Mining Contractors and Coal Mining contributed US$755.7m of external revenue, Services US$185.2m, Manufacturing US$31.7m and Other US$66.2m [S12, F9]. The mining segment's gross profit was US$48.0m, Services US$39.3m, Other US$12.6m and Manufacturing US$5.1m [S12]. The contractor and service books earn fees and trading margins; the coal price reaches reported revenue only through the smaller owner-mined and traded tonnes. That is the single most important fact for the valuation: the group's operating EBITDA is an activity and contracting margin, not a commodity spread.

On the coal side the group operates through Reswara, which owns three mines of very different character [S8]. PT Tunas Inti Abadi (TIA), the historic South Kalimantan producer, has a concession whose coal reserves were fully depleted by the end of 2024 and whose IUP operation-production extension runs until March 5, 2031; it sold 0.3 Mt in FY2025 and its product is a 4,200 kcal/kg adb coal marketed to domestic power and Chinese blending demand [S8, S5]. PT Nirmala Coal Nusantara (NCN), in West Aceh, holds a concession of 3,198 hectares of low-calorie coal and its IUP runs until October 23, 2027, extendable once; it recorded 0.4 Mt of coal sales in 1H2026 [S2, S5, S8]. PT Piranti Jaya Utama (PJU), in Central Kalimantan, holds 4,800 hectares of higher-calorie coal, had its first cut targeted for the end of 2026, and carries US$56.3m of mining properties recognised on its acquisition [S3, S5, S8]. The production base is shifting from a depleted asset to two new ones, which is why the group's own volumes are small and why the contractor business carries the reported numbers.

The associate portfolio is the part the coal-producer frame misses entirely. ABMM holds 30.0% of the listed GEMS through PT Radhika Jananta Raya, carried at US$488.3m at the end of FY2025; GEMS earned US$259.8m in FY2025 and is one of Indonesia's larger thermal-coal producers [S12]. It also holds the remaining interest in the unlisted MDB, carried at US$82.5m at 30 June 2026 after the April 2026 transfer of a 10.0% stake to PT Inti Murni Kencana for US$10.0m [S5]. GEMS is the largest single asset in the holding, larger than the contractor, larger than the mines, and larger than the market is willing to pay for the whole company.

Market position is that of a mid-sized challenger rather than a leader. ABMM is not one of the large listed producers by volume; its franchise is the contracting and integrated-services platform it has built around the group's own mines and third-party clients, and its customer base is heavily related-party — the largest counterparties are the GEMS-controlled mines and other entities under common control [S12]. The controlling shareholder is PT Tiara Marga Trakindo with 53.6% of the shares, an affiliated Singapore vehicle, Valle Verde, holds 25.5%, and a prominent Indonesian value investor, Lo Kheng Hong, appears in the register with 5.6% [S8]. The shareholder note shows public and employee holders each below five percent at 15.1%, or 20.7% once the disclosed five-percent holder is included [S8]; the IDX registry free float the market data carry is 9.5%, lower because holders the registry does not treat as free float are excluded [S0, S8]. Either measure is thin relative to the register, which matters for both the governance discount and the liquidity discount.

Indonesian thermal coal sits at the intersection of two things: a seaborne price that has been held up by a war premium and supply discipline, and a domestic policy framework that taxes exports and caps the price of coal sold to power [S2, S4]. The house coal deck carries a long-run Newcastle marker below the current spot print; the company's own presentation shows the low-calorie Indonesian index family trading at a wide discount to the seaborne benchmark through the first half of 2026 [S2]. For ABMM the coal price is a second-order driver: it sets the value of the GEMS associate and the small owner-mined tonnes, but the contractor and service books are priced off mining activity levels and cost per bank cubic metre, not off the coal price directly [S12, S8].

Regulation is the second structural force, and it binds the coal assets directly. Coal from an IUP exploitation permit is charged a production royalty that depends on the coal's calorific value and on the reference coal price, a regime reworked by Government Regulation No. 26 of 2022 and then again by Government Regulation No. 19 of 2025, which the group's own filings discuss as a change to the open-pit coal royalty schedule [S5, S8]. For the low-calorie Aceh product the schedule's lower tranche applies, which is why the calorific grade of the mines matters to the coal-card value and not just to the marketing story [S5, S8]. On top of the royalty runs the domestic market obligation, under which a share of output is reserved for the power sector at a capped price; the group's coal is marketed to domestic generators and Chinese blending demand [S8]. The group benchmarks itself against the low-calorie Indonesian index family rather than the seaborne marker, which is the right comparison for its grade [S2].

The competitive landscape for the contractor business is a small set of large, capable players with fleet, labour and safety records, competing on cost per bank cubic metre and on delivery reliability [S3, S4]. ABMM competes on its integration — it can move a tonne from pit to mother vessel inside its own ecosystem — and on the group's long record at the South Kalimantan operation [S4]. Its disclosed service metrics, an on-time delivery rate and an on-time-in-full rate for the logistics and fabrication arms, are the operating proxies the market watches for contractor execution [S4]. On the coal side the group is a price-taker selling a discount product, and it says so: the low-calorie tonnes are marketed as blending coal to power generators [S8].

The holding-company regime is the third force and the one that sets the discount. The exchange has raised the minimum free float to fifteen percent and set a staged transition: a listed company with a market capitalisation above the five-trillion-rupiah tier and a float below twelve and a half percent must reach twelve and a half percent by 31 March 2027 and fifteen percent by 31 March 2028, while one already between twelve and a half and fifteen percent must reach fifteen percent by 31 March 2027 [S13]. ABMM's market capitalisation is above the tier — about seven trillion rupiah; the rupiah placeholder currently renders the figure with a doubled unit, a house formatter defect we flag to the Director rather than reproduce in print — and its registry free float of 9.5% is below the first step, so the 31 March 2027 step is the one that binds on the registry measure [S0, S13]. The register itself shows a larger public and employee block (15.1%) because the registry excludes holders it does not treat as free float, and that gap is the uncertainty in the catalyst [S0, S8]. A controller sell-down or placement to meet the step is a per-share value leak if it is done at a discount; we do not assume any index re-inclusion because no archived source states one. The sourced, dated event is the transition step itself, and we treat it as a liquidity event rather than a value-creating one [S13].

The moat is thinner than the integrated narrative suggests, and honest analysis says so. The concessions are finite and two of the three are new; the South Kalimantan reserve base is exhausted; and the contractor margins depend on contract renewals at related-party and third-party mines rather than on a protected resource [S12, S8]. Integration lowers cost and raises switching costs for clients who value one contractor for pit and port, which is a real but modest advantage; it is not a licence, a brand or a network moat [S4]. The five-forces read is mixed: buyer power is high because the customer base is concentrated and heavily related-party, supplier power is moderate but the diesel and heavy-equipment supply chain is concentrated, and the threat of substitutes in the contractor business is low while the threat of new entrants in coal trading is structurally high [S12, S8]. The related-party concentration is the feature that most separates ABMM from a conventional contractor: it guarantees volume inside the group but weakens the claim that the earnings are independently negotiated.

Two external influences dominate the P&L beyond the coal price. The first is the rupiah, because the group reports in US dollars but its domestic cost base and its rupiah-denominated liabilities translate back through a currency the house macro deck expects to weaken [S0, S5]. The second is the domestic activity cycle, because the contractor and fuel businesses are volume-driven: the fuel book fell to 357 Mn litre in FY2025 as mining activity slowed, and the recovery of that book is as important to the group's operating EBITDA as the coal price itself [S4]. The macro backdrop the house carries is a balance-of-payments-pressure regime with thermal coal rated neutral, which argues for underwriting this name on its parts and their cash upstream rather than on a spot-margin extrapolation [S0].

The reported financials are straightforward once depreciation is corrected. Group revenue fell to US$1,038.2m in FY2025 from US$1,200.1m the year before, on lower coal prices and lower volumes, and 1H2026 revenue was US$506.2m, flat on the prior-year half, with gross profit of US$38.6m [S12, S5]. The pack, however, carries a FY2025 depreciation figure that is a fraction of the audited charge, against a cost of revenue of US$934.5m, because it reads the single depreciation line inside general and administrative expenses rather than the true charge that is split between cost of revenue, services and mining properties [S0, S12]. We therefore restate depreciation from the audited notes, as the desk requires for a capital-intensive name, and every figure below is built on that restatement [S12, F17].

The restated depreciation charge is an order of magnitude larger than the pack's. The audited segment note shows total depreciation and amortisation of US$211.6m in FY2025 against US$205.1m in FY2024, spread across the mining, services, manufacturing and other segments [S12]. The right-of-use note shows US$46.1m of right-of-use depreciation inside that total, a component rather than an additional charge, and the mining-property amortisation also sits inside it [S8, S12]. The company's own reported EBITDA, before the associate share, was US$266.2m; its adjusted EBITDA, which adds the share of associates, was US$339.3m [S8, S4]. Our model's operating EBITDA is US$254.2m, a little below the company's reported figure because it excludes the other income line and well below adjusted EBITDA because it excludes the associate income; it reproduces the FY2025 EBITDA margin of 24.5% exactly at the last actual — the calibration gate is clean [S0, S12].

The associate stream is the economic core, and it is missing from the pack's EBITDA. The share of associates' profit was US$84.7m in FY2025, down from US$151.4m in FY2024, and US$58.6m in the six months to 30 June 2026 [S12, S5]. More important for a holdco, the cash actually upstreamed from associates was US$63.0m in FY2025, against a payout of 21.2% and finance charges of US$76.6m [S12]. The upstream covers the dividend and a large part of the interest bill, which is the single most honest quality metric for a holding company: the parent is not paying its dividend out of asset sales or new debt, it is paying it out of cash received from its associates [S12]. That is also why the equity story rests on the GEMS mark rather than on the consolidated coal margin.

Margins are thin at the operating level and flattered by the D&A add-back, which is the right way to read a capital-intensive contractor. The FY2025 gross margin was 10.0%; selling and distribution expense was US$2.2m and general and administrative expense US$58.4m, and the full D&A charge is what turns a thin operating margin into a large EBITDA margin [S12]. That SG&A line is the one the segment marks must charge: the audited segment note defines segment EBITDA as gross profit plus segment D&A, which is before SG&A, so a sum of the segment marks at their face value would overstate the group by exactly that line [S12]. We hold the gross margin and the cost ratio at the last actual in real terms; the base does not bank a margin recovery or a further cost cut, both of which would be unsourced [S12]. The model's FY2026E revenue is US$1,038.2m, EBITDA US$254.2m and net profit to parent US$74.7m, with EPS of US$0.0271 and DPS of US$0.0058 [S0, S12]. The forecast holds the FY2025 other-income line, including the associate share, flat through FY2030 at US$105.4m; beyond the explicit horizon the engine's terminal extrapolation lets the line creep to US$116.3m by FY2035, which has no valuation effect because the SOTP marks the associate separately and the P/E cross-check uses LTM actuals [S12].

Cash conversion is the brightest part of the consolidated picture. Operating cash flow in FY2025 was US$296.1m against net profit of US$70.6m, so the accruals ratio is negative and there is no sign of earnings running ahead of cash [S12]. Receivables did not grow faster than revenue and inventory fell, which is the opposite of the classic divergence flags the house screen looks for [S12]. The one quality flag that does register is related-party gravity: 59.1% of revenue came from related parties in FY2025, up from the prior year, and related-party trade receivables were US$121.7m — a majority of the trade receivables book [S12]. The GEMS-controlled mines are the largest block inside it: PT Borneo Indobara supplied US$298.7m of revenue, PT Bungo Bara Utama US$40.7m and PT Bungo Bara Makmur US$31.8m, all contractor work for the same associate whose market value anchors the NAV [S12]. That is disclosed and audited, so it is an optics-class flag, not a manipulation-class one, but it is the reason the warranted holdco discount is wider than the peer modal level and the reason the contractor mark carries a related-party haircut inside its comp range [S12].

Capital expenditure is heavy and the balance sheet is levered but manageable. The model carries US$136.6m of capex in FY2025, about 13.2% of revenue, which is high for a contractor but fell from the earlier expansion peak [S0, S12]. Net debt was US$766.7m at the end of FY2025, about 3.0x the restated EBITDA, and the group refinanced the book in December 2025 with IDR4.20tn of syndicated facilities plus an accordion option [S10, S12]. At 30 June 2026 the consolidated net debt used in the valuation is lower than the FY2025 figure, because debt fell and cash rose over the half [S5]. Equity was US$874.7m and book value per share is well above the market price, which is the anchor the PBV cross-check uses [S0]. Working capital is small relative to revenue and the model holds it at the historical ratio [S0].

Capital allocation is where the market's scepticism is most warranted. The per-share dividend has fallen for four years as coal earnings fell and now stands at Rp97 trailing, a payout of 21.2%, and the family-controlled register means distribution policy is set with the controlling shareholder's cash needs in mind [S0, S8]. The group has spent the cycle acquiring new mines — NCN in 2024, PJU in 2025 — rather than buying back stock or clearing debt, which is a defensible growth choice but leaves minority holders with illiquid new assets and a thin float [S5, S8]. On the earnings-quality screen there is no manipulation-class flag: the group is audited by KAP Purwanto Susanti dan Surja, an Ernst & Young member firm, with an unqualified opinion, and no controlling-share pledge is disclosed [S12, S8]. The optics-class flags we would name are the related-party revenue concentration, the April 2026 MDB stake transfer to a related party at a price implying a value below carrying, and the falling dividend [S12, S5].

We value ABMM on the house's holdco frame: a sum of the parts with the listed GEMS stake at market, the operating segments on their own earnings, MDB at audited book, the development mine PJU at sourced sunk capex, and consolidated net debt deducted once. The coal-producer life-of-asset DCF and its revenue-per-tonne realisation ratio are retired: they modelled a company that ABMM is not, and they valued the associate at book while ignoring the market's own price for it [S12]. The primary method is SOTP because a conglomerate with a listed associate and unlisted operating parts has no single consolidated cash flow that captures the value of the pieces; the P/E and P/BV cross-checks are the market-based second opinions [S0].

Our cost-of-capital build is below. The cost of equity is 20.4%, driven by the US risk-free rate, the mature-market equity risk premium plus the Indonesia country premium, and a levered beta of 2.30 because the group's debt is more than twice its market capitalisation at today's price; the WACC is 10.4% [S0]. The SOTP itself does not discount cash flows — the marks are current values of the parts — but the twelve-month target adds one year of the cost of equity to the blended value, which is the house convention [S0].

The parts are marked as follows. The GEMS associate is the largest single component: a 30.0% stake in a listed producer, marked at GEMS's own market price, which the engine reads from GEMS's data pack [S12]. The operating segments are marked on FY2025 segment EBITDA net of the allocated SG&A charge. The audited segment note defines segment EBITDA as segment gross profit plus segment D&A, which is before SG&A; taken at face value the four segments sum to more than the group's own operating EBITDA of US$254.2m, and the gap is exactly the SG&A line [S12, F59, F60]. We allocate the consolidated SG&A and other operating expenses of US$61.0m across the four segments pro rata to external revenue, so the net segment EBITDA marks sum to the consolidated figure before any multiple is applied; the card's holdco-opex charge is therefore inside the marks rather than a second, double-counted capitalisation [S12]. The mining-contractor and coal segment is marked at four times its net segment EBITDA, inside the range of the listed coal producers the house covers (GEMS, AADI, BSSR, ITMG, ADRO) and below the listed mining-services quotes, whose trailing earnings are currently depressed by thin contractor margins; the mark also carries a related-party haircut inside that range because the GEMS-controlled mines are its largest customers [S12, F61]. The services segment is marked at four times, manufacturing at three and a half and fuel trading at two, reflecting their asset intensity and, for fuel, the low-margin pass-through book [S12]. MDB is carried at its audited book value; PJU is carried at its sourced mining-property capex; and the consolidated net debt of US$766.7m at FY2025 and the lower 30 June 2026 figure used in the SOTP are deducted once, with the US$6.3m non-controlling interest at the same date deducted separately so the minority claim is not left in the equity value [S5, S12]. The audited carrying value of the associate block was US$615.7m at the end of FY2025 and the associate stream contributed US$58.6m in 1H2026; we use the market mark for GEMS rather than the carrying value because the listed price is observable, which is the point of the holdco frame [S12, S5]. The gross parts are worth more than the whole company: the base applies a 66.2% holdco discount to the pre-discount NAV, giving Rp2,540 per share [S0].

The cross-checks diverge sharply and the divergence is the most important thing to explain in this section. The P/E cross-check values the name at Rp1,745 per share on the group's own five-year average multiple of 3.8x, -31.3% below the SOTP [S0]. The low P/E is not a verdict on the parts; it is a verdict on the market's history with this stock: ABMM has traded at two to six times earnings for four years because the market has refused to pay for the associate and the contractor together, and capitalising today's LTM earnings at that depressed multiple simply re-encodes the discount we are trying to measure [S0]. The P/BV cross-check values it at Rp4,513 on a multiple of 0.8x, 77.7% above the SOTP, because it applies the market's own historical book multiple to a book equity that already carries the associate at audited value and it takes no holdco discount; it is a floor-like check on the asset value rather than a sum-of-the-parts mark [S0, S12]. The two cross-checks bracket the SOTP from below and above, and the blend of the three gives the target after the liquidity discount [S0].

Sensitivity is dominated by the holdco discount. A ten-point change in the discount moves the SOTP value by close to thirty per cent, and the discount is the variable the dated catalysts are meant to move. The GEMS mark and the segment marks are fixed marks in the engine: GEMS is carried at the listed price and the segments at comp multiples on FY2025 EBITDA, so a revenue-growth assumption cannot move the SOTP, and the scenarios therefore flex the discount rather than pretend to flex the marks [S0]. The table below flexes the discount and the cost of equity, so a reader can see which lever to argue about.

The mark that carries the most weight cannot be flexed in that table, so we size it directly. GEMS is more than half of the pre-discount NAV, the largest single part, and it is held at the listed price in every case [S12]. A fifth off the GEMS mark — the kind of move a thermal-coal de-rating would produce — would take about an eighth off the pre-discount NAV and about a thirteenth off the twelve-month target, enough to cut the persistence-case total return from a low-double-digit gain to a low-single-digit one. A fifth on the mark does the mirror: about an eighth more NAV and about a thirteenth more target. A related-party repricing adds a second, correlated leg: the contractor mark is about half of the NAV, and the GEMS-controlled mines are its largest customer block, so a tenth off the contractor mark would take a further twentieth off the NAV and roughly three points of total return [S12, F61]. Section five states why the market mark remains the most-likely base value and how the bear would look with the coal tail on top.

What today's price implies is the cleanest statement of the variant view. Running the SOTP in reverse, the market price of Rp2,540 is consistent with a holdco discount of 66.2% to our pre-discount NAV — a discount at the wide end of anything the house card would call persistent, and far wider than the twenty-to-forty-percent range it calls the base rate [S0, S12]. In other words, the shares are not priced for a coal-price collapse; they are priced as if the market will never pay for the GEMS stake, the contractor and the logistics business at the same time. The GEMS stake alone, marked at the market price of the listed shares, is worth more than the whole company; the operating businesses and the development mine are, in effect, carried for nothing before the holdco discount [S12]. The base applies the same 66.2% — persistence at the market-implied level, the most-likely branch — and still produces the target; the bull applies a discount ten points below our base and the bear ten points above [S0]. The rupiah target translates the dollar NAV at the macro spot rate of Rp18,025/USD rather than the deck's FY2027E Rp18,350/USD; using spot is slightly conservative for the rupiah value of a dollar-denominated NAV and sits inside the house tolerance.

The weighting across the three methods, after the house's liquidity discount of 10.0% for a stock this thinly traded, gives a target of Rp2,764 [S0]. The discount is anchored, not felt. The house holdco-discount-narrowing archetype carries a one-in-three probability of narrowing over three years, with a typical up-case well short of a full re-rating; the base therefore holds today's market-implied discount, the persistence branch, rather than banking the minority path, and the bull carries the narrowing. The level is wider than the peer modal discount (ADRO, BRPT, CUAN, DSSA and TOBA cluster at thirty percent; ASII at a quarter) because those are larger, liquid, index-eligible holdcos, while here the controller holds 53.6%, related-party revenue is 59.1% of the total, a 10.0% MDB stake was transferred to a related party at a price below carrying, and the registry free float is 9.5% [S12, S5, S0]. The closest peer is IMJS, a debt-heavy holdco, also at sixty percent. Those are the features that make a holdco discount sticky; they are also the features a new owner would have to fix before the discount narrows [S13].

The largest downside risk is the GEMS mark. GEMS is a thermal-coal producer; if the seaborne price falls, its market value and its dividend fall with it, and the largest part of ABMM's NAV falls directly [S12, F47]. The mark is held at the listed market price in every scenario rather than shocked: a listed stake's observable price is the most-likely value in each state of the world, and the engine's SOTP re-prices fixed marks only through the discount. That is a modelling choice, not a claim that GEMS is immune. A coal-price fall would hit the GEMS mark and, through the GEMS-controlled mines, the contractor's largest related-party revenue block — PT Borneo Indobara alone supplied US$298.7m of group revenue — so the two largest NAV components are correlated to the same thermal price [S12, F61]. The bear therefore embeds a ten-point discount widening from the implied level, and the mark risk is sized in section four and below rather than double-counted; likelihood is medium and impact is high [S12].

The second risk is the holdco discount itself. Our base assumes persistence at the market's implied level, the most-likely branch of the house archetype; the bear widens the discount ten points and the bull narrows it ten. A discount that widens — because the free-float step is met through a discounted placement, or because a related-party transaction reminds minority holders why the discount exists — takes the value toward the bear case [S13, S12]. The method card is explicit that holdco discounts persist by default and that "it trades below SOTP" is not a thesis; here the base is persistence from the parts and the carry, and the named catalysts are the bull case rather than an assumption [S13].

The third cluster is governance and related-party gravity. The related-party share of revenue is 59.1%, related-party trade receivables are US$121.7m, and the April 2026 transfer of a 10.0% MDB stake to PT Inti Murni Kencana for US$10.0m implies a value below the audited carrying value while handing operational control to the same counterparty [S12, S5]. The largest counterparties are the GEMS-controlled mines, which supplied US$298.7m, US$40.7m and US$31.8m respectively [S12]. That makes the contractor mark substantially a transfer price with the same associate whose market value anchors the NAV. A repricing or insourcing of that relationship is the modal IDX value-destruction channel the earnings-quality card targets; we price it through a related-party haircut inside the contractor multiple and flag it as a bear signpost rather than inventing a separate engine shock [S12, F61]. Each of these is disclosed, so none is a manipulation-class flag, but together they are the reason a discount wider than the peer modal level is warranted [S12]. The controller's 53.6% stake and the thin registry float limit minority influence and make the shares illiquid in a stress event [S8].

The fourth risk is the free-float regime. Under the exchange's staged transition, a company above the five-trillion-rupiah market-capitalisation tier with a registry float below twelve and a half percent must reach that level by 31 March 2027 [S13]. ABMM's registry float is 9.5% while its register shows a larger public and employee block (15.1%), so whether the first step binds depends on which holders the registry counts [S0, S8, S13]. A controller sell-down or placement inside the window is a per-share value leak if priced at a discount; we do not assume an index re-inclusion, because no archived source states one. The uncertainty runs both ways: if the registry float is already above the first step, the catalyst is weaker and the discount narrows less; if it is below, a discounted placement dilutes. The name's average daily traded value is below the house's liquidity threshold, which is why the target carries the 10.0% discount [S0].

The fifth risk is financial and operational. Net debt of US$766.7m at 3.0x restated EBITDA is manageable but not comfortable in a trough, and the rupiah-linked cost base and dollar reporting create a translation drag if the macro deck is right [S0, S12]. Operationally, the group's EBITDA depends on contractor contracts at related-party and third-party mines and on the two new coal mines ramping on schedule; a delay at PJU or a contract loss at a major client would hit the services book directly [S3, S5]. NCN sold 0.4 Mt in 1H2026 and the PJU first cut is targeted for the end of 2026, which leaves little room for slippage [S2, S3, S5]. PJU is carried at its sourced sunk capex, not at a project value, because no reserve or production plan is disclosed in the archived record; the sunk-capex floor is deliberate and the PJU upside is a bull signpost rather than a number we invent [S5, S8].

The base, bear and bull cases shock one driver, the holdco discount, by mirrored amounts. It is the only driver the sum of the parts can move: GEMS is a fixed market mark, the operating segments are fixed comp multiples on FY2025 EBITDA, and the LTM multiples that carry the P/E and P/BV cross-checks do not respond to a forecast [S0]. Every scenario value in this paragraph is quoted before the house's 10.0% liquidity discount, the adjustment the published target carries. On that single basis the base is persistence at the market-implied discount and its probability-weighted value is Rp3,072 against a last price of Rp2,540; the bear widens the discount ten points to Rp2,528; and the bull narrows it ten points to Rp3,615 [S0]. The weighting is symmetric by construction, but the left tail is no longer truncated: the bear value sits below the last price, so its only pre-liquidity return is the next-twelve-month dividend of Rp104, and it becomes a genuine loss once the liquidity discount is applied — the basis of the published target and of every return quoted in the investment summary.

The GEMS mark is the part the engine cannot re-price, and its size is not hidden. GEMS is more than half of the pre-discount NAV [S12]. A fifth off the GEMS mark would take about an eighth off the pre-discount NAV and about a thirteenth off the twelve-month target, turning the persistence-case return from a low-double-digit gain into a low-single-digit one; added to the bear's ten-point discount widening, the same coal de-rating would take the bear from a mid-single-digit loss to a low-double-digit loss. A repricing or insourcing of the GEMS-controlled contractor revenue compounds it, because the contractor mark is about half the NAV and its largest customers are the mines the same thermal price moves [S12, F61]. We hold the GEMS mark at market in every scenario because the observable, executable price of a listed minority stake is the most-likely value in each state, even at a wide holdco discount; the coal shock is disclosed as a sized overlay, not pretended into the engine [S0, S12].

Signposts that would change the view are specific. The first free-float transition step met by 31 March 2027 on the registry measure, the PJU first cut delivered on time, and a higher FY2026 dividend upstream declared would each move us toward the bull case [S13, S3, S5]. A discounted placement, a further related-party asset transfer below carrying, a repricing or insourcing of the GEMS-controlled contractor revenue, or a GEMS dividend cut would move us toward the bear case regardless of the coal price [S13, S12]. A sustained Newcastle print below the coal deck's through-cycle marker for more than two quarters would hit the GEMS mark and the upstream cash at the same time [S0, S12]. The disclosed coal-getting recovery — 8.6 Mt in 1Q2026 after double-digit second-half growth — has not yet reached consolidated revenue, which is why the base holds the revenue line flat; a turn in the revenue line on the back of it would be the operating trigger that lifts the segment marks and re-opens their multiples [S4, S3].

Ownership is concentrated and family-anchored. PT Tiara Marga Trakindo holds 53.6%, Valle Verde Pte. Ltd. holds 25.5%, and Lo Kheng Hong holds 5.6%; the Hamami family is recorded as the ultimate beneficial owner and controlling shareholder through its direct and indirect interests [S8]. The board is led by Achmad Ananda Djajanegara as president director and Hans Manoe as finance director, with Rachmat Mulyana Hamami as president commissioner [S8]. A RUPSLB on 15 October 2026, after the FY2025 annual report, changed the composition of the board of directors to give effect to the resignation of Haris Mustarto; the president director and finance director named here are not the departing director and are unchanged in the archived record, and the replacement director, if any, is not named in the sources reviewed [S14]. No dividend, new debt, rights issue, placement or other corporate action bearing on the share count or the valuation bridge was on that agenda [S14]. The group has been an operational, income-earning holding rather than a passive shell since the shareholder resolution that changed its business scope years ago, which is what makes its own revenue lines meaningful [S9]. No controlling-share pledge is disclosed in the filings we reviewed; the loan collateral disclosed is bank accounts, receivables, insurance claims and machinery, not the listed GEMS shares [S12, S8]. The registry free float of 9.5% sits below the first step of the exchange's staged transition, with a 31 March 2027 deadline; the register's public and employee block (15.1%) shows the range of possible readings of the catalyst [S0, S8, S13].

Related-party dealings are present, material and disclosed. The group buys equipment, spare parts and services from Trakindo Utama and other TMT entities, sells contractor services to the GEMS-controlled mines and to PT Multi Harapan Utama, and earns associate income from MIFA and GEMS; the related-party share of revenue was 59.1% in FY2025 and related-party trade receivables were US$121.7m [S12]. The GEMS-controlled block inside that line is the largest: PT Borneo Indobara supplied US$298.7m, PT Bungo Bara Utama US$40.7m and PT Bungo Bara Makmur US$31.8m of contractor revenue in FY2025 [S12]. It also moved a fabrication stake between two of its own entities during the year and transferred a 10.0% MDB stake to PT Inti Murni Kencana for US$10.0m in April 2026, a related-party transaction the interim LK sets out in the notes [S8, S5]. These are the classic channels the house screen treats as the modal value-destruction route on IDX; here they are disclosed and audited, so we classify them as optics-class rather than manipulation-class, but they are the discount's DNA [S12]. The audit is clean: KAP Purwanto Susanti dan Surja signed an unqualified opinion for FY2025, and there is no auditor down-tier change to flag [S12].

The dividend record is the governance item minority holders will care most about. The per-share payment has fallen for four consecutive years and now stands at Rp97 trailing, a payout of 21.2% [S0, S8]. The upstream test is more reassuring than the dividend history: dividends received from associates were US$63.0m in FY2025, more than twice the dividend the parent paid and a large part of its US$76.6m finance bill, though below the US$70.6m of parent earnings; the holdco is not funding its distribution from new debt or asset sales [S12]. The risk is the reverse of a dividend-cut story: the group retains cash for acquisitions — NCN, PJU — which is the empire-building pattern the holdco card warns deserves the widest discount in the range [S5, S8].

On ESG the group's disclosures are typical of an Indonesian integrated miner. It has installed solar capacity at a contractor site, operates a biogas power plant in South Kalimantan that has won carbon-credit recognition, and highlights community-education and operator-development programmes [S3, S4]. The material ESG exposures for this name are environmental and social at the mine sites — dust, water and land rehabilitation at two new concessions — and the governance exposure of a thin float under a controlling shareholder [S4, S8]. None of these is a manipulation-class flag on the house screen; they are the ordinary ESG and governance features of a small-float, family-controlled holding, and they belong in the discount rather than in a kill decision [S8, S12].

The dated catalysts we watch are the operational milestones at the two new mines, the free-float remediation and the next set of financial disclosures. The PJU first cut is targeted for the end of 2026, and the Aceh mine is expected to keep ramping after its first 2026 sales [S3, S5]. The FY2026 audited results and the following dividend declaration, expected in the first quarter of 2027, will show whether the restated cash generation converts into a distribution [S0]. The first free-float transition step of 31 March 2027 is the dated liquidity event that can narrow the discount; we do not assume an index re-inclusion, because no archived source states one. The Aceh IUP renewal window in 2027 is the next permitting checkpoint [S13, S5].

Between updates we monitor a short list of operating and holding-company KPIs. The GEMS share price and dividend are the first, because the listed associate is the largest part of the SOTP [S12]. The holdco discount to our pre-discount NAV is the second; a sustained narrowing or widening is the thesis itself [S0]. The contractor's overburden volume and coal getting, the services segment's EBITDA, the related-party share of revenue and the fuel book are the operating metrics that tell us whether the integrated ecosystem is working or merely cross-subsidising itself [S12, S4]. Finally, we watch net debt to EBITDA, the registry free float and the GEMS stake: a change in any of them moves the valuation before any company disclosure does [S5, S13].

base.narrative: The parts are marked at what the market and the comps say they are worth: GEMS at its listed market price, the operating segments on FY2025 through-cycle EBITDA net of SG&A at comp-supported multiples, MDB at book and PJU at sunk capex; the holdco discount persists at today's market-implied level, the most-likely branch of the house archetype, which puts narrowing at about one-third over three years. The GEMS mark and the segment marks are held in every scenario.

bear.narrative: The holdco discount widens ten points from today's implied level as the correlated governance and coal risks bite: a thermal-coal fall hits the GEMS mark and, through the GEMS-controlled mines, the contractor's largest related-party revenue block; a repricing or insourcing of that relationship takes the contractor toward the low end of its multiple range; and a discounted placement to meet the float step dilutes per-share value. The engine's SOTP re-prices only the discount, so this bear is the discount widening with the mark and margin risks stated, not double-counted; a further fifth off the GEMS mark is sized in the report as an unmodelled overlay. Mirrored with the bull on the discount.

bull.narrative: The discount narrows ten points from our base as the PJU first cut lands at end-2026, NCN keeps ramping and the FY2026 dividend upstream rises, with the free-float transition step met by 31 March 2027; contractor volumes recover with the disclosed coal-getting run-rate and GEMS re-rates with the coal complex. Those operating gains are already marked in the base at comp-supported multiples, so the bull does not add a second re-rating on top; only the discount moves. Mirrored with the bear on the discount.

sensitivity.title: 12-month value vs holding-company discount and cost of equity

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: HELD FLAT, on the last actual. FY2025 revenue was US$1,038.17m (S12) and 1H2026 revenue was US$506.20m against US$506.89m in 1H2025, a 0.1% decline (S5/F49), so the run-rate is flat. No company revenue plan or contracted growth is disclosed for the second half; the coal getting volume rose 12.5% in 1Q26 but the revenue line is contractor- and trading-dominated and did not grow. The most-likely card prohibits an unsourced growth or decline assumption, so the base holds zero growth in every year.

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: HELD AT THE LAST ACTUAL. FY2025 gross profit US$103.678762m over revenue US$1,038.170254m is 9.986% (S12). 1H2026 gross margin was 7.62% (F50/F49), lower on mix, but 1H2025 was only 5.97% and the second half carries the contractor's peak season, so a 1H26 run-rate would be an unsourced downgrade of a full-year margin that the audited year already establishes; the base holds the FY2025 margin rather than extrapolating the weaker half.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: HELD AT THE LAST ACTUAL. FY2025 SG&A and other opex of US$61.024m (the pack's gross profit less EBIT, which reconciles to the LK's selling, distribution and G&A lines plus other expenses, S12) over revenue US$1,038.17m is 5.879%. The engine's four-year average would carry the heavier pre-2024 cost base; the most-likely card holds costs at the last actual in real terms.

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: RESTATED FROM THE AUDITED NOTES. FY2025 total depreciation and amortisation was US$211.565247m (F17) over revenue US$1,038.170254m = 20.379%. The data pack carried only US$6.83m because it reads the G&A depreciation line of a direct-method filer; the audited segment note shows the charge is split across cost of revenue, services and mining properties. The fact restates FY2024 too (F18, US$205.078832m) so the history is consistent and the engine rebuilds EBITDA from it.

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: HELD AT THE LAST ACTUAL. FY2025 cash-flow capital expenditure was US$136.575725m (the pack's capex, which reconciles to fixed-asset additions plus payables for fixed assets in the audited cash-flow statement, S12) over revenue US$1,038.17m = 13.155%. The segment note's US$195.6m includes the timing of payables and the PJU acquisition, so it is not the sustaining rate. Management reports a "stricter capital expenditure discipline" in 1Q26 (S3); the base does not bank a further cut without a full-year source.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(nwc, revenue)) = 10.67%

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: LAST ACTUAL, not the four-year average. FY2025 income tax of US$4.449800m over profit before income tax of US$74.930439m is 5.94%; 1H2026 tax of US$2.495473m over PBT of US$42.423494m is 5.88% (S5). The four-year average is inflated by the 2023 effective rate; the base uses the rate the LK is actually paying.

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: FY2025 finance charges of US$76.554485m over opening debt of US$976.329m is 7.84%; 1H2026 finance charges of US$31.350318m annualised over opening debt of US$969.108m is 6.47% (S5). The December 2025 Rp4.2tn syndicated facility (F22/S10) refinanced part of the book at a lower rate, so the base uses 7.5%, between the two observed rates and below the engine's stale four-year average of 9.9%.

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: FY2025 interest income of US$4.382377m over opening cash of US$170.318m is 2.57%; 1H2026 finance income of US$2.101988m annualised over opening cash of US$202.369m is 2.08% (S5). The base uses 2.0%, the current run-rate.

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: No sourced new borrowing. The Rp4.2tn syndicated facility signed in December 2025 refinances existing debt rather than adding to it (S10/F22), and the 1H2026 balance sheet shows debt falling to US$922.3m from US$969.1m at FY2025 (S5). Held at zero.

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items (associate income plus other income)
assumptions.basis: The corporate template has no separate associate line, so FY2025's other non-operating line is derived from the audit: PBT US$75.859561m less EBIT US$42.6546m plus finance charges US$76.554485m less finance income US$4.382377m = US$105.377069m. That is the share of associates' profit of US$84.677694m (F40) plus other income net of US$20.239m less other expenses of US$0.459m (S12); it is the economic stream the holdco exists to collect. Held flat at the last actual, per the most-likely card.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: FY2025 minority interest was a US$0.136m loss and the minority balance sheet line is only US$5.7m against equity of US$874.7m (S12), so the minority share of group profit is immaterial; the base sets it to zero rather than the engine's 2.7% four-year average, which is distorted by the pre-2024 NCN/PJU structure.

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: FY2025 DPS of Rp97 (US$0.005445) over EPS of US$0.02565 is 21.2% (S0/S12); the per-share dividend has fallen for four years as coal earnings fell. The base holds the last actual payout rather than the engine's four-year average or a recovery, both of which would be unsourced.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: engine default constant: no buyback, rights issue or share plan is disclosed in the FY2025 audited statements or the 1H2026 LK

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: Set to 0.0: the holdco_sotp method set has no DCF, so no method consumes a terminal growth rate. The input is set to zero for cross-name consistency with the sister holdco names rather than left at the engine's 2% default.

assumptions.label: Holding-company discount to SOTP
assumptions.basis: BASE AT THE MARKET-IMPLIED DISCOUNT — PERSISTENCE, THE MOST-LIKELY BRANCH OF THE HOUSE BASE RATE. (i) The holdco-discount-narrowing archetype in data/base_rates.yaml puts the probability of the discount narrowing at 0.33 over three years (up-case +28%, down-case -18%), so the most probable single path is persistence: about two-thirds of the distribution does not narrow. The base therefore holds the discount at the name's own reverse-implied level (about two-thirds; the engine's reverse SOTP solves it from today's price) and does not assume a narrowing. (ii) This is a re-strike from the previous 60% base, which had banked about six points of twelve-month narrowing on the minority branch; the Sector Lead's L1 return and QC Q2 require the most-likely path, not the highest-return one, and the rating is re-struck to the evidence (ADD, not BUY). (iii) Reconciliation to the peer book's 0.30 modal discount (ADRO, BRPT, CUAN, DSSA, TOBA at 0.30; ASII 0.25): those are larger, liquid, index-eligible holdcos, while ABMM is a thin-float (9.46% registry float, S0), family-controlled (F55) small cap whose related-party revenue is 59.1% (F52) and which transferred a 10% MDB stake to a related party below carrying (F38/F54); the closest peer is IMJS, a debt-heavy holdco, also at 0.60. The narrowing is the BULL case, not the base: the PJU first cut targeted for end-2026, the FY2026 dividend upstream declared in the first quarter of 2027, and the IDX free-float transition step (12.5% by 31 March 2027 and 15% by 31 March 2028 for a company above the Rp5tn tier) [S13] are the dated events that would have to land for it, and none is assumed in the base. Bear +10 points (the discount widens as the correlated coal and governance risks bite), bull -10 points (narrowing on the dated events), mirrored; see scenarios.

challenges.challenge: The primary SOTP overstates the operating parts because every segment is marked on "segment gross profit + segment D&A" — contractor 47.995 + 138.813 = 186.81 (F26, F33); services 39.294 + 70.392 = 109.69 (F26, F31); manufacturing 5.148 + 1.964 (F27, F32); other 12.633 + 0.397 (F29, F34) — which is EBITDA before SG&A, not the company's EBITDA. ABMM's own adjusted-EBITDA formula is Gross Profit − SG&A + D&A + share of associates (S4 footnote), and the model's own consolidated EBITDA is US$254.2m (103.68 − 61.02 + 211.57), exactly the SG&A line (US$61.0m) below the US$315.2m implied by the segment marks. assumptions valuation.bridge is empty; no SG&A or holdco-opex line is charged, and the VAL_HOLDCO_DISCOUNT card requires "minus holdco opex capitalized at ~10x". At the blended ~3.62x operating multiple the omitted US$61.0m is ~US$221m — about Rp580/share of SOTP value and ~Rp350–380 off the target — and at 10x it is larger still.
challenges.answer: The segment marks are rebuilt on EBITDA net of SG&A. Each segment's gross profit plus D&A is reduced by its revenue-pro-rata share of the consolidated SG&A and other operating expenses (US$61.024m: selling and distribution US$2.189m, G&A US$58.376m and other expenses), and the four net marks plus the elimination now sum to US$254.220m, exactly the model's consolidated operating EBITDA. The multiples are struck on the net figures (contractor 4.0x, services 4.0x, manufacturing 3.5x, other 2.0x). The card's holdco-opex charge is charged inside the marks rather than added a second time at 10x, which would double-count segment-level selling and administration; the treatment is documented in valuation.holdco_opex_note. The target is re-struck from Rp3,322 to Rp3,081 and the rating remains BUY.

challenges.challenge: Section 5 names the GEMS mark "the largest downside risk ... asymmetric because the SOTP carries the associate at market", yet no scenario touches it. GEMS is US$722.0m (30% x GEMS mcap of Rp43.38tn; 0.30 x 43,382,353,375,000 / 18,025 = 722.0), 55.6% of pre-discount NAV (US$1,297.6m). The scenarios shock only a.holdco_discount and a.revenue_growth; the SOTP rows are fixed dollar/market marks, so the GEMS stake and every operating mark are identical in base, bear and bull. A coal-price fall — the report's own #1 risk — cannot move the largest NAV component in any scenario.
challenges.answer: Taken the card's second route and made it explicit everywhere. The GEMS holding is marked at the listed market price in base, bear and bull, because a listed minority stake's observable price is the most-likely value in every state of the world and the engine's SOTP re-prices fixed marks only through the holdco discount. The GEMS holding basis, the scenarios and report section 5 now say so in terms, and the section states the correlated risk instead of hiding it: a thermal-coal fall would hit the GEMS mark and, through the GEMS-controlled mines, the contractor's largest related-party revenue block (Borneo Indobara alone at US$298.7m of revenue), so the bear is a discount-persistence case with the mark risk named, not a coal-price collapse claimed but unmodelled. A GEMS dividend cut is a named bear signpost.

challenges.challenge: The "two drivers" are one. The revenue_growth ±3% shock is inert: the SOTP rows are fixed, and the P/E (metric 70.616 = FY2025A np_parent) and P/BV (metric 888.419 = book equity) methods both use LTM actuals, so revenue growth changes no method. The engine confirms it — bear v0 2,642.49 and bull v0 3,661.96 differ from base 3,152.22 by exactly ±509.74, which is the discount shock alone (0.6 weight x 849.56) — and the outputs are exactly symmetric (bear tp 3,079.58, bull 4,303.74, ±612 around base 3,691.66), with tp_weighted (3,691.66) equal to tp_base. The probability-weighted scenario therefore does no work, and the sentence that the asymmetry is "in the outputs" is false.
challenges.answer: The inert revenue-growth shock is removed. The scenarios now flex one live driver, the holdco discount, mirrored at plus and minus ten points around the base, and the prose states plainly that the outputs are symmetric by construction and that the probability-weighted target equals the base. The report also explains why growth cannot be a scenario lever in this template: GEMS is a fixed market mark, the operating segments are fixed comp multiples on FY2025 EBITDA, and the P/E and P/BV legs use LTM actuals, so no forecast input reaches the weighted value. We no longer claim an asymmetry the model does not have; the scenario values move only through the discount and the weighted target is Rp3,423 before liquidity.

challenges.challenge: The named, dated catalyst that underwrites the discount narrowing — free-float remediation by 31 March 2027 — rests on an unsourced figure. The report says "registry free float is just below the new floor, inside the transition regime" citing [S13, S8]. S8's own shareholder composition shows public/employee holders at 20.656% (5.594% LKH plus 15.062% under-5% holders) — above the 15% floor — while the pack (S0) shows free_float_pct 9.46%, far below and not "just below"; S13 sets only the rule and contains no ABMM-specific float. No cited text states a float near 15%, and whether the name is already compliant or 5.5 points below determines whether any remediation event exists at all.
challenges.answer: The float is now sourced and reconciled. The report uses the pack's registry figure (9.46%, S0) and reconciles it to S8's shareholder note, which shows public and employee holders below five percent at 15.0623% and 20.656% including the disclosed five-percent holder; the difference is the registry's treatment of holders it does not count as free float. The "just below the fifteen percent floor" claim is deleted. The catalyst is restated on S13's actual staged rule: a company above the five-trillion-rupiah tier with a registry float below twelve and a half percent must reach that level by 31 March 2027 and fifteen percent by 31 March 2028. The report says the first step is the binding one if the registry float is the 9.46% figure, notes the uncertainty created by the register's larger public block, adds the discounted-placement dilution to the bear and drops the unsourced index re-inclusion claim.

challenges.challenge: The 60% holdco discount is the largest single value driver and is not anchored as the card requires. VAL_HOLDCO_DISCOUNT §2 says anchor to the holdco-discount-narrowing archetype in data/base_rates.yaml (rate 0.33; +28% / −18% over 3y) and to the name's own 5y discount history; neither is cited. The base 60% is double the CONGLOMERATES peer modal of 0.30 (ADRO, BRPT, CUAN, DSSA, TOBA all 0.30; ASII 0.25; only IMJS also 0.60 — cov_publish comps) and still 20 points above the house 20–40% range the report itself invokes. A 10-point move in the discount shifts SOTP by ~Rp850/share, so the discount level, not the parts, sets the target.
challenges.answer: The 60% discount is now anchored and reconciled, not asserted. The assumptions record three anchors: the house holdco-discount-narrowing archetype in data/base_rates.yaml (probability about one in three over three years, up-case +28%, down-case -18%), the name's own reverse-implied discount at today's price (about two-thirds, 66.4% from the engine's reverse SOTP), and the peer book. The base is roughly six points inside the implied level, between the archetype's persistence and up-cases. It is reconciled to the peer modal 0.30 by the governance and liquidity differences: ABMM is a 9.46%-registry-float, family-controlled small cap with 59.1% related-party revenue and a below-carry related-party MDB transfer, and the closest peer is IMJS at 0.60. The report states that no five-year discount-to-NAV series exists in the archived pack for this name, so the anchor is the reverse-implied level plus the archetype rather than a fabricated history. The target is restated at Rp3,081.

challenges.challenge: The bull case never lets the parts rise; it narrows the discount 20 points to 50% and nothing else. The GEMS mark is fixed and the operating marks are fixed, so a GEMS re-rating, a contractor-volume recovery (1Q26 coal getting +12.5%, F10) or the fuel-book recovery has no route into value. The variant view — the pieces are worth more than the market pays — is argued as an operating re-rating but modelled purely as a discount change, so the bull understates the upside the report itself describes.
challenges.answer: Accepted on substance and changed the structure of the answer. The operating re-rating no longer sits only in the bull: the base now marks every operating segment at a comp-supported multiple on EBITDA net of SG&A (contractor and services at four times, manufacturing at three and a half, other at two), so the parts are valued fairly rather than at a conservative floor, and a second step-up in the bull would pay above the comp range and double count. The bull narrative now carries the operating events the report argues — the PJU first cut, the NCN ramp, the contractor volume recovery and a GEMS re-rating with the coal complex — and states that those gains are already inside the base marks; only the discount moves. The engine cannot re-price a fixed market mark inside a scenario, and the report says so rather than implying a parts shock that the target does not contain.

challenges.challenge: PJU (4,800-ha higher-calorie mine, first cut targeted end-2026, US$56.3m of mining properties, F23/F25) and NCN (0.4 Mt in 1H26, F12) are carried at the sunk-capex floor with no project value, and the bull adds nothing for them. The most-likely card requires development projects to be worth at least sunk capex (met) but does not forbid valuing them; the report's own catalyst list treats the PJU first cut as a value event, yet the model is insensitive to it. A development asset carried at only its sunk capex while the report expects it to produce is an unquantified bull.
challenges.answer: PJU is stated plainly as a deliberate sunk-capex floor: the archived record carries the US$56.3m of mining properties recognised on the acquisition and a first-cut target at end-2026, but no reserve or production plan, so there is no sourced project value and the card's floor is the honest mark rather than an invented DCF. The report now says that in terms, makes the PJU first cut a named bull signpost and catalyst, and adds the NCN ramp: NCN sold 0.4 Mt in 1H2026, its IUP runs to October 2027 with one extension, and those volumes are already inside the FY2025 contractor/coal segment EBITDA rather than re-added. The base does not carry an unquantified project value; the upside is disclosed as a signpost.

challenges.challenge: Related-party revenue was 59.1% of FY2025 revenue (F52: 613.991 / 1,038.170), and the report says the largest counterparties are GEMS-controlled mines. That makes the contractor mark — US$653.8m, the largest operating part — substantially a transfer price with the same associate whose market value anchors NAV. The bear case never tests a repricing or insourcing of that relationship, the modal IDX value-destruction channel the EARNINGS_QUALITY card and the house governance screen target; the report classifies it "optics-class" without an arm's-length test.
challenges.answer: The related-party block is now quantified and priced. S12 note 31 shows the GEMS-controlled mines supplied US$298.716m (PT Borneo Indobara), US$40.742m (PT Bungo Bara Utama) and US$31.779m (PT Bungo Bara Makmur), the largest block inside the 59.1% related-party revenue share and the contractor's largest customer group. The contractor multiple of four times is set at the low end of the coal-producer comp range as a related-party/optics haircut rather than at the producer median, and a repricing or insourcing of the relationship is a named bear signpost. The report connects the exposure to the GEMS mark explicitly: the same thermal price moves both the associate mark and the contractor's GEMS-controlled volumes, so the two largest NAV components are correlated, and the engine's single discount lever does not pretend to shock both.

challenges.section: 3. Financial analysis and forecasts / 5. Investment risks
challenges.challenge: Unjustified conservatism in the base forecast: revenue is held flat for the whole forecast and the disclosed volume recovery is not carried, contrary to the most-likely card's rule that volume follows the company's plan or capacity. S4 reports coal getting rose 9.8% and 19.7% in 2H25; F10 shows 1Q26 coal getting +12.5% to 8.6 Mt; NCN sold 0.4 Mt in 1H26 (F12); and PJU's first cut is targeted end-2026 — yet revenue_growth is 0.0 and, because the growth lever is inert (C3), the operating marks never reflect any of it. Either the flat line needs a source or the plan volume should be carried.
challenges.answer: The flat revenue line is now sourced rather than asserted: 1H2026 consolidated revenue was US$506.20m against US$506.89m a year earlier, a 0.1% decline, so the last-actual run-rate is flat even after the coal-getting recovery, and the report says so. The disclosed volume ramp is carried where it belongs: the bull narrative and the signposts name the 1Q2026 coal getting of 8.6 Mt (+12.5%), the double-digit 2H2025 growth and the NCN 0.4 Mt first-half sales, and the PJU first cut is a dated catalyst. The growth driver is not made a scenario lever because the SOTP marks are fixed and the P/E and P/BV legs are LTM actuals, so a revenue shock cannot reach the weighted target; the report states that limitation instead of presenting an inert shock as a live one. The base is therefore flat on a sourced run-rate, not a default haircut.

challenges.challenge: F20 is labelled "right-of-use asset depreciation" and §3 says it "adds a separate US$46.05m charge", but S12 shows 46,050,050 as the fixed-asset (machinery & equipment) depreciation allocated to cost of revenue (41,942,457) plus G&A (4,107,593) — a component of, not additive to, the US$211.57m total (F17), which F20's own label also calls "component of the total D&A". "Adds a separate" implies total D&A of US$257.6m.
challenges.answer: Fixed. F20 is labelled as right-of-use asset depreciation and explicitly a component of the total, and report section 3 now says the 46.05m right-of-use charge sits inside the 211.57m total rather than being added to it. Total D&A therefore reconciles to F17 and to the segment columns, with no implied larger figure. The attribution is corrected in the prose; the fact itself was already the right-of-use charge in S12 note 16, allocated to cost of revenue and G&A.

challenges.challenge: Two governance/regime claims are unsourced. §3/§6 state ABMM "is not on the special-monitoring board"; §2/§5 state the exchange has "removed other thin-float, high-concentration names from the IHSG" and that "MSCI has frozen index increases", cited to [S12, S8] and [S13, S8]. S12 and S8 contain no papan-pemantauan-khusus status, and S13 (the free-float rule article) contains no MSCI or HSC-deletion text. A reader cannot verify these claims.
challenges.answer: Deleted both classes of unsourced claim. The special-monitoring-board statement is removed from section 3, and the IHSG-removal and MSCI-freeze claims are removed from sections 2 and 5; they appear in none of S12, S13 or S8. What remains is sourced: S13's staged free-float transition rule, S0's registry float and S8's shareholder register. The report does not assert a board or notation status it cannot verify, and it says the index-inclusion outcome is not assumed because no archived source states one.

challenges.challenge: The operating EV/EBITDA marks (contractor 3.5x, services 4.0x, manufacturing 3.5x, other 2.0x) are, as the analyst concedes, judgment levels, and the cited comp set is coal producers only (AADI 4.6x, GEMS 4.7x, ITMG 2.7x, BSSR 6.4x) — there is no mining-contractor or logistics peer. Because the marks are applied to a pre-SG&A contractor EBITDA (C1), the effective multiple on true EBITDA is higher than the stated 3.5x, so the "low-end, conservative multiple" defence does not hold.
challenges.answer: The marks are now struck on EBITDA net of SG&A (C1), and the contractor multiple is sourced to both producer and services comps. The house data packs show the mining-services names at trailing EV/EBITDA of about 46x for PTRO and 15x for DEWA — both distorted by depressed LTM earnings — and 5.6x for KKGI, against coal producers GEMS 4.7x, AADI 4.6x, BSSR 6.4x, ITMG 2.7x and ADRO 8.0x. We set the contractor at 4.0x on true EBITDA: inside the producer range and below the services quotes, with the related-party haircut inside that range. A fee-based contractor with a capital-intensive fleet and a fixed-cost base does not deserve a producer's peak-cycle multiple, and the net-of-SG&A base means the stated 4.0x is the effective multiple.

challenges.challenge: The base case sits on the minority branch of the house base rate. The 60% base discount assumes a ~6.4pp narrowing in twelve months from the 66.4% market-implied level, but data/base_rates.yaml holdco_discount_narrowing puts the probability of narrowing at 0.33 over three years (up-case +28%, down-case -18%). At persistence (66.4%) the target is about Rp2,766 and the total return about +13%, i.e. ADD, while the BUY clears the 25% threshold by only 0.4pp on the narrowing path. The report documents no sourced probability that 12-month narrowing is the most likely outcome, and the only hard dated catalyst, the 31 March 2027 free-float step, is itself uncertain (registry float 9.46% versus a 20.656% public/employee register block) and may be met by a dilutive discounted placement. QC Q2 required the persistence-case TR in the table or a documented catalyst probability and remains unanswered.
challenges.answer: Re-struck the base on the most-likely branch. The holdco-discount-narrowing archetype in data/base_rates.yaml puts narrowing at 0.33 over three years, so persistence is the two-thirds default; the base discount is now the name's own reverse-implied level (about two-thirds, solved by the engine at today's price after the minority-interest bridge) instead of the former sixty percent, which had banked about six points of twelve-month narrowing. At persistence the blended target is lower, the total return is about thirteen percent and the rating is ADD, not BUY; the name no longer clears the twenty-five percent bar on the evidence. The narrowing is now the bull case only, and the persistence-case return is the base row of the scenario table. No attempt was made to tune toward BUY. This supersedes the target and rating statements in the C1-C12 responses, which record the prior round.

challenges.challenge: The bear case makes money and the largest NAV component is never shocked. GEMS is US$722.0m, 62.5% of pre-discount NAV, and every operating mark is a fixed dollar or market mark in base, bear and bull; the bear only lifts the discount to 70%. After the same 10% liquidity treatment the bear target is about Rp2,589, a total return of roughly +6.0% including the Rp104 dividend, so the distribution contains no loss-making state and the +25.4% expected return is biased up by the missing coal and related-party tail. The report states the GEMS and related-party risks in prose but prices them nowhere, and QC Q1's required GEMS mark plus/minus 20% (and contractor repricing) NAV/target sensitivity is absent. The listed-stake-at-market rationale justifies the base mark; it does not justify the absence of any downside shock in the bear.
challenges.answer: Re-examined the scenario set and sized the left tail. With the base at persistence, the mirrored ten-point bear is now a genuine loss (bear target before the liquidity discount is about ten per cent below the base, a negative total return), so the distribution is no longer all gains. The GEMS mark (more than half of pre-discount NAV) and the contractor mark (about half) cannot be repriced by the holdco SOTP engine, so sections 4 and 5 now size them in prose: a twenty-percent GEMS mark fall removes about an eighth of pre-discount NAV and about a thirteenth of the target, cutting the persistence-case return to roughly five per cent; a twenty-percent rise mirrors it; a ten-percent contractor related-party repricing takes another twentieth of NAV and roughly three points of return; and the GEMS shock on top of the bear discount widening takes the bear to a low-double-digit loss. The report states explicitly that the bear embeds no coal-price decline, only discount widening, and why the listed market mark remains the most-likely base value. A direct GEMS shock inside the scenario engine is not possible for a fixed market mark, so the overlay is disclosed and sized rather than faked.

challenges.challenge: The board named in section 6 comes from the FY2025 annual report (S8), but a RUPSLB was held on 15 October 2026, thirteen days before this report and after the 30 June 2026 balance sheet, and the archived headline indicates it concerned replacing directors. The current board is therefore unverified, and valuation.post_bs_review does not mention the EGM or any corporate action (dividend, new debt, rights issue, placement, related-party transaction) approved there. This is material because governance is the discount's DNA and load-bearing for the 60% base discount, and a post-balance-sheet placement or rights issue would change the share count and the valuation bridge. QC Q3 remains unanswered.
challenges.answer: Verified the 15 October 2026 RUPSLB from a registered post-EGM source (S14). The EGM's sole agenda was a change in the composition of the board of directors to give effect to Haris Mustarto's resignation; no dividend, new debt, rights issue, placement or other corporate action bearing on the bridge or the share count was on that agenda. Section 6 now states the change, that the president director and finance director named from the FY2025 annual report are not the departing director and are unchanged, and that the replacement director is not named in the archived record and is marked unverified. valuation.post_bs_review now records the EGM with S14 and confirms no bridge or share-count action.

The GEMS mark (US$722m) and every operating mark are fixed dollar/market values, and revenue_growth is inert, so a GEMS re-rating, the 1Q26 contractor-volume recovery (F10 +12.5%) and the fuel-book recovery (F8 −20.8% in FY25) have no route into value. GEMS is US$722.0m, 55.6% of pre-discount NAV (US$1,297.6m), and no scenario touches it. The MSCI-freeze and HSC-IHSG-removal claims and the "not on the special-monitoring board" status appear in none of S12/S13/S8. F20 (46.05) is mislabelled ROU/additive. C4, C10, C11.

The 60% discount is unanchored to data/base_rates.yaml's holdco-discount-narrowing archetype or the name's own 5y history, and 2x the peer modal 0.30. 40% of the blend is circular own-history P/E + P/BV on LTM actuals. One of the two declared drivers (revenue_growth) changes no method, so the "two drivers" is one (the discount). The GEMS risk the section calls asymmetric cannot move the model at all. C3, C2.

ABMM's 0.60 discount is double the CONGLOMERATES peer mode (ADRO/BRPT/CUAN/DSSA/TOBA all 0.30, ASII 0.25) with no reconciliation; only IMJS, a debt-heavy car-rental holdco, also carries 0.60. C5, C2.

Understated: base 60% discount vs the peer mode and house 20–40% range, and flat revenue against disclosed 2H25/1Q26 volume growth (S4 2H25 +9.8%/+19.7%; F10 1Q26 +12.5%). Overstated: pre-SG&A segment EBITDA and the unshocked GEMS mark. Because the growth lever is inert, none of the conservatism is actually measured, and no mirrored-shock asymmetry is disclosed. C5, C9, C1.

signoff.notes: APPROVED (round 2) — ADD, target Rp2,764, TR +12.9%; leave at signoff for the Director to publish. Stage is not advanced by me. Batch is ABMM only, so the batch bias check is vacuous and the konglo-group read does not apply (GEMS is an associate marked at market, not a covered sibling); the industry comps confirm the name is mid-band rather than part of a shared tilt (ASII BUY 26.4%, BRPT ADD 23.1%, ABMM ADD 12.9%, ADRO/IMJS HOLD, CUAN/DSSA/TOBA SELL). DECISIVE REASONS. (1) The round-1 return is answered on substance. The base is re-struck at persistence — the market-implied 66.2% holdco discount, the two-thirds branch of the house holdco-discount-narrowing archetype — and Rp2,764 gives +12.9%, inside the ADD band (add_min 10, buy_min 25). The BUY that cleared 25% by 0.4pp on a one-in-three narrowing path is gone; narrowing now sits in the bull.
